Residual_RH and Residual_GH_mean are strongly correlated (r = -0.58), so a causal link is likely, which rules out D.

The data can't settle the direction on its own, so I chose it on physical grounds. Geopotential height reflects the large-scale circulation. High geopotential height brings subsidence and drier air, which lowers relative humidity. Relative humidity has little effect back on the large-scale height field. That favors B over A, and a two-way relationship (C) is less likely. I did not run a causal-discovery test, so this rests on domain reasoning rather than a statistical test.

ANSWER: B
